The key to this mechanism is understanding that my ranking only affects which school I get *within* my "Obtainable Schools" set. It doesn't change *what* schools are in that set. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to simply rank the schools according to my true preferences. This is because, no matter what my obtainable set is, ranking my preferences truthfully ensures that I will get the best school possible *within that set*.

For example, suppose my Obtainable Schools are {x, z}. If I rank y > x > z > w, I will get x. If I rank z > x > y > w, I will get z. If I rank x > z > y > w, I will get x. So, no matter what, my true preferences are the best guide.

Therefore, I will rank the schools according to my true preferences: y > x > z > w.
